lost_facts.assertion: test_r1.py::test_rule__a_versioned_checkpoint_rewritten_after_every_appended_response - probe error: TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not TurnLedger (raised inside sidecar_path() when the test calls write_sidecar(str(tmp_path), ledger))
lost_facts.evidence: The agent implemented `def write_sidecar(ledger: TurnLedger, working_dir: str) -> str` (transcript line 4541) and `def verify_sidecar(ledger: TurnLedger, working_dir: str)` (line 4560) - ledger first, working_dir second - while its own `sidecar_path(working_dir)` and `read_sidecar(working_dir)` take working_dir alone. The oracle solution instead defines `write_sidecar(working_dir, ledger)` and `verify_sidecar(working_dir, ledger)` (working_dir first, oracle.patch lines 834/850), and test_r1.py line 127 calls `write_sidecar(str(tmp_path), ledger)` positionally, which binds `ledger=str(tmp_path)` and `working_dir=<TurnLedger>` under the agent's signature, crashing inside `os.path.join`. Grepped every remark that mentions write_sidecar (g7.r1.l4, l6-area/say20, l15, fix27, fix28) plus the requirement table itself: none states the parameter order. Nothing in the corpus - chat, mail, or wiki - ever shows a call site or signature for write_sidecar/verify_sidecar, so there was no way to infer which of the two equally-plausible orderings the grader expects.

search_strategy: Systematic but keyword-bound. Code was read first (curator source tree), then Gitea PR 685 comments (empty), then BookStack via /api/search with a handful of terms ('ledger','COMPLETION_SENTINEL','multi-turn agent','seed message','curator+agent','next_speaker','status tracker') which surfaced 7 pages (139,143,144,150,152,210,211); each was fetched whole via /api/pages/{id} (comments included) - good practice per the world's own hint about comments not being indexed - but page 211 was only ever read via `head -60`, truncating its later comments (missed g7.r2.g7r2-l10), and page 210 was fetched to /tmp/p210.txt but never read at all. The 'stop-marker-matching' page (carrying g7.r2.g7r2-l07) was never found by any search term tried and never enumerated directly, so it was never seen. Mail was searched with a SINGLE IMAP TEXT query for the literal word 'ledger' (12 hits, all of which were read in full) - this missed three threads whose bodies never use the word 'ledger' (g7.r1.l9, g7.r2.g7r2-l08, g7.r2.g7r2-l05), even though all three are squarely about the ledger/stop-check design.
